extracted.intended_audience: book reviewers, editors, and publicists (especially those interacting with The New York Times Book Review)
extracted.subtask_short: NYT book review selection and standards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines describing which books the NYT Book Review prioritizes for coverage and the standards that constitute a strong review (what good reviews include, common mistakes, reviewer selection, and formats). Intended to guide editorial selection and reviewer practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection volume / triage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High incoming volume means editors must prioritize; selection factors (below) are used to triage which books get reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major publisher
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books from established imprints are more likely to be selected for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Established author
rubrics_metrics.description: Established author — known names get reviewed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author prominence increases chances of placement and coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debut buzz
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highly anticipated debuts (pre-publication buzz) attract editorial attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prize potential
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books viewed as likely award contenders are prioritized for review and coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural moment alignment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books that align with or speak to an ongoing cultural moment are more newsworthy for coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject significance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books that address important or significant subjects are more likely to be selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original argument / approach
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonfiction or critical works that present an original argument or novel approach are favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-genre crossover appeal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books that cross genres or have crossover appeal can be attractive to editors for broader readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation events
rubrics_metrics.description: Translation events — major international author into English
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable translations of major international authors into English are prioritized as significant publishing events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posthumous releases
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works published posthumously by significant figures warrant consideration for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre-defining works
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books that define or redefine a genre are especially newsworthy for coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse voices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An increasing editorial emphasis on diverse voices shapes selection decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bestseller / commercial significance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercially significant books or bestsellers may be selected due to reader interest and cultural impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good review should engage both the reader's emotions and intellect; it should be lively and thoughtful rather than flat or purely informational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Depth and context — what else is on the subject; what writer's done before
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should situate the book within broader conversations: other works on the subject, the author's previous work, and relevant historical or cultural context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific examples and quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific examples and quotations from the book
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete examples and quoted passages to demonstrate claims about the book's strengths or weaknesses rather than making unsupported assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style description
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the writing style and voice of the author; explain how style contributes to the book's effects and merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific judgment — what works, what doesn't
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give evaluative, specific judgments about the book's successes and failures rather than vague praise or criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worth-it determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Worth-it determination — should reader read this
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly convey whether the book is worth reading and for whom; help readers decide if they should spend time on it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflating review with book report
rubrics_metrics.description: Common mistake: Conflating review with book report
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A review should analyze and evaluate, not just recount the book's contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid plot summary instead of analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Common mistake: Plot summary substituted for analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimize plot summary; prioritize analysis of themes, craft, argument, and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid spoilers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reveal key plot twists or information that would ruin the reading experience; if necessary, warn or negotiate spoilers carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic praise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague, unsubstantiated praise ('wonderful', 'riveting') without examples to back it up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic criticism without examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Common mistake: Generic criticism without examples
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't make broad negative claims without pointing to specific passages or elements that illustrate the problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author prominence drives placement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-profile authors often determine the prominence and placement of reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical importance of subject
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects that are timely or of widespread public interest make a book more likely to be reviewed and prominently placed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of argument (nonfiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit: Originality of argument in nonfiction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonfiction, originality of thesis or approach is a key factor in both selection and evaluative judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft / style (fiction)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In fiction, attention to craft and distinctive stylistic choices are central criteria for assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to cultural conversation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the book contributes meaningfully to ongoing cultural or intellectual conversations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place in genre / oeuvre
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the book's relation to its genre and to the author's body of work; consider significance within those contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer qualifications matter
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer's expertise and background affect both selection of reviewers and credibility of the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length matched to significance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The length of the review should correspond to the book's significance and complexity (long lead reviews vs. briefer pieces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer subject-matter expertise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose reviewers with relevant expertise for the book's topic, genre, or cultural context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of past reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer selection: Quality of past reviewing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past demonstrated quality in reviewing is a criterion for selecting reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from author
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer selection: Independence from author (no friends)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid assigning reviewers who have close personal or professional relationships with the author to prevent conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse voices among reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer selection: Diverse voices among reviewers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for diversity among reviewers to reflect varied perspectives and backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long lead reviews (format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Format: Long lead reviews (front of book)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-depth, front-of-book features for major titles that merit extended analysis and prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefer reviews (format)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorter reviews placed within review sections for books of moderate interest or significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capsule reviews (format)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very short capsule reviews for quick recommendations, often used in paperback roundup or column-style presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor's Choice list (format)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curated lists highlighting select books recommended by editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year-end lists (format)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roundups and best-of lists that place books in the context of the year's publishing and cultural conversation.
